name: React Interview Questions
title: React Interview Questions
description: Prepare for your React job interview with our list of common questions and answers. Cover key topics from JSX basics to advanced hooks, and boost your confidence for that big day by reading detailed explanations!

modules.name: JSX basics
modules.description: JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript used in React. It allows you to write HTML-like code in your JavaScript files, making it easier to describe the structure of UI components.

modules.name: Components and props
modules.description: Components are the building blocks of React applications, and props are the mechanism for passing data between components. Understanding how to create and use components, as well as how to work with props, is fundamental to React development.

modules.name: State management with useState
modules.description: The useState hook is a way to add state to functional components in React. It allows components to manage and update their own data, enabling dynamic and interactive user interfaces.

modules.name: Conditional rendering
modules.description: Conditional rendering in React allows you to show or hide elements based on certain conditions. This topic covers various techniques for implementing logic-based rendering in your components.

modules.name: Lists and keys
modules.description: Rendering lists efficiently is a common task in React applications. This topic covers how to render arrays of data and the importance of using keys for optimal performance and correct behavior.

modules.name: Event handling
modules.description: Event handling in React involves managing user interactions with your application. This topic covers how to attach event listeners to elements and handle various types of user input.

modules.name: Lifecycle methods (class components)
modules.description: Lifecycle methods are special methods in class components that run at particular times in a component's life. Understanding these methods is crucial for managing side effects and optimizing performance in class-based components.

modules.name: Hooks (useEffect, useContext, useRef)
modules.description: Hooks are functions that let you use state and other React features in functional components. This topic covers several important hooks that handle side effects, context, and references to DOM elements.

modules.name: Forms and controlled components
modules.description: Handling forms in React often involves creating controlled components where form data is handled by the component's state. This topic covers techniques for managing form inputs and submissions in React applications.

modules.name: React Router
modules.description: React Router is a standard library for routing in React applications. This topic covers how to implement navigation in single-page applications, including route configuration and navigation between different views.

modules.name: Context API
modules.description: The Context API provides a way to pass data through the component tree without having to pass props down manually at every level. This topic covers how to create, provide, and consume context in React applications.

modules.name: Higher-Order Components (HOCs)
modules.description: Higher-Order Components are a pattern for reusing component logic. This advanced topic covers how to create and use HOCs to enhance components with additional functionality.

modules.name: Render props
modules.description: Render props is a technique for sharing code between React components using a prop whose value is a function. This topic covers how to implement and use the render props pattern for flexible component composition.
